plan.title: Treatment-specific time-course DE beyond shared trend
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2-condition x 4-timepoint bulk RNA-seq design (salmon gene counts, 3 reps/cell, 25 samples total incl. metadata rows, 12000 genes). The research question — which genes change over time in a treatment-specific manner, beyond the trend shared by both conditions — is precisely the DESeq2 time-course likelihood-ratio-test (LRT) design: fit the full model ~condition + time + condition:time against the reduced model ~condition + time. Genes significant in this LRT have a time trajectory that differs between conditions, independent of any main effect of time common to both. Because condition:time is a difference-of-differences with only 3 replicates per cell, the LRT (and the per-timepoint Wald simple-effect contrasts reported beside it) has real but limited power; this is stated explicitly rather than compensated for by loosening thresholds. QC precedes modelling to catch mislabeled/outlier samples before they distort the interaction estimate. Reference gene sets present in the environment (MSigDB Hallmark, GO BP/CC/MF, Reactome, WikiPathways, MSigDB canonical) support both a pre-ranked GSEA on the full gene list (primary, since only a handful of genes may pass the interaction threshold at n=3) and, if the significant list clears ~50 genes, a GO/goseq over-representation follow-up as the knowledge-base's permitted enrichment set requires for this design. The DE gene table is clustered by per-timepoint shrunken log2FC trajectory to answer 'which genes' at the level of coherent temporal patterns rather than a flat list, per DESeq2 time-course reporting practice.

constraints: Universe = the genes that passed the pre-filter and were tested by DESeq2, never the whole genome/annotation
Run only if the significant interaction list has >=50 genes; otherwise report list size and explicitly skip
caveats: GO terms are nested; expect blocks of correlated significant terms rather than independent findings even after rrvgo reduction

grounding.reason: ORA/enrichGO with rrvgo reduction is a permitted method per the knowledge check, gated by the >=50-significant-gene rule (R-0103) and using the tested-gene universe (R-0046).

steps.name: Reproducibility record and consolidated report
steps.question: What is the final, reproducible summary of which genes and pathways show a treatment-specific time trajectory beyond the shared time trend, with all methods, versions, thresholds, and power caveats stated?
acceptance_criteria: Report states: package versions (DESeq2, apeglm, fgsea, clusterProfiler etc.), design formula and each contrast with named reference levels, alpha=0.05 threshold, number of genes tested/filtered/significant at each stage, gene set collection names and versions

Interaction (treatment-specific trajectory) results, per-timepoint simple effects, and enrichment results presented side by side with the stated power limitation for n=3/cell reiterated in the executive summary
sessionInfo() (or R equivalent) and random seeds for any stochastic step (fgsea permutations) captured and stored with the results
steps.context: Final synthesis step consolidating T1 (DE/clustering) and T2 (enrichment) outputs into one reproducible report.
constraints: Do not present the interaction gene list as a complete accounting of treatment-specific genes; explicitly state that a gene's absence from the list at n=3/cell is not evidence of no effect

grounding.reason: Consolidated report step follows the standard reporting checklist: method/version/design/thresholds/counts (R-0041), reproducibility record (R-0086), interaction+simple-effects side by side (R-0092), stated power caveat (R-0094), and enrichment reporting fields (R-0051).
